function.name: emit_sidecar_verdict
function.arguments: {"verdict": "revise", "reason": "The requirement said to preserve the documented consumer output formats while migrating to quote_order. Your diff changed the documented output shapes: web.checkout now returns {\"currency\": ..., \"total_minor\": ...} instead of the documented {\"total\": ...}, and jobs.export/export now returns \"currency,total_minor\\nUSD,1230\\n\" instead of the documented \"total\\n2.50\\n\". You also deleted the legacy \"test_legacy_consumers\" assertions and rewrote them to match the new shapes, which is regression evidence rather than proof of preservation. Please keep the original documented output formats byte-for-byte (checkout -> {\"total\": <number>}, export -> \"total\\n<amount>\\n\", receipt/summary strings unchanged) and derive them from the Quote (e.g. via quote.total_minor / format_minor and CURRENCY_EXPONENTS), rather than altering the observable contract. Then re-run python -m pytest -q tests and add tests that pin the original documented formats.", "suggestedFix": "Restore the documented consumer output shapes (web.checkout {\"total\": ...}, jobs.export \"total\\n<amount>\\n\", cli.receipt/mobile.summary strings) computed from the central Quote's total_minor, keep currency/discount as keyword-only options, and pin the legacy formats in tests."}

function.name: emit_sidecar_verdict
